# v2.74 — make it yours

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v2.73-dev** and **v2.74-dev**.

Training Tracker can now wear your organisation's name, logo and colours. Everything is set from **Admin → System Settings → Branding**, stored in the database, and applied the moment you save — no reinstall, no config file to edit, no service restart.

It also fixes three faults in backup and restore, one of which has been stopping backups from downloading at all.

## What's new

**Your name, everywhere it matters.** Set an application name and it replaces "Training Tracker" on the login screen, in the sidebar, in the browser tab, on the About page — and in the entry your users see in their authenticator app when they enrol in MFA.

**Your logo.** Upload a PNG, JPEG, WebP or ICO (up to 512 KB) and it replaces the shield icon on the login, first-run setup and MFA-enrolment screens. Leave it empty and the built-in shield stays.

**Your favicon.** Upload a PNG or ICO (up to 128 KB) for the browser tab icon. Square, at least 32×32, works best.

**Your colour.** Pick a brand colour and every accent in the app follows it — buttons, links, focus rings, active tabs, the selected navigation item — in both light and dark mode. Pick something light and you'll get a warning, because buttons put white text on that colour. Charts and PDF exports deliberately keep their own palette, so your reports stay readable.

**A tidier login screen.** The logo and the name can each be switched off on the login page. Turn off the name if your logo already includes it, or turn off both for a plain sign-in form; the header spacing adjusts so nothing is left floating.

**The name can come off the browser tab too.** A separate switch leaves the tab untitled, so the browser shows the address instead of a name. For deployments that want no product name visible anywhere, rather than a different one.

**Reset to defaults** puts the name, colour, logo and favicon back to stock in one click. It doesn't touch any of your data.

## Changed

**The version number no longer appears on the login screen.** It's the one page someone can reach without signing in, and it doesn't need to advertise which version you're running. You can still see it in the sidebar footer and on the About page.

## Fixed

**Backups were failing to download.** Since offerings became company-scoped, both the full and configuration backup downloads had been failing with a server error. If you have been unable to take a backup recently, this is why, and it now works again. **Take a fresh backup after updating.**

**Configuration backups were quietly losing your settings.** Restoring one only ever restored the date format — your session timeout and public-API switch were silently dropped and reverted to defaults. All settings now come back with the archive, branding included.

**Restored settings appear immediately.** Settings are briefly cached for performance, and a restore didn't clear that cache — so for up to half a minute after a restore the app kept showing the old values. It now refreshes straight away, and the same applies after a full wipe.

## Notes

- The update applies two database migrations. The update script handles this for you; there is nothing to run by hand.
- An install with no brand colour set renders exactly as it always has — the standard palette is used unchanged, not an approximation of it.
- Branding is included in configuration backups, so it travels with your catalogue when you seed a new system. A full **Wipe** resets it to the defaults.
- Uploads are checked by inspecting the file's actual content rather than trusting what the browser reports, and **SVG files are refused** — an SVG can carry scripts, which isn't a risk worth taking for a logo.
- On browsers older than roughly 2023 the app falls back to its standard blue palette. Everything else works normally.
